Frequently Asked Questions

Can I Buy Without Customization?

Add standard styles to your enquiry. We confirm availability, specifications and pricing before you order.

How Do I Request Custom Or Bulk Pricing?

Choose Add to Enquiry, add reference styles to your enquiry list and share your project requirements. You can also enquire without selecting a product.

What Is The Minimum Order Quantity?

MOQ depends on product and technique. Include your target quantity so the applicable minimum can be confirmed. The quantity selector is not an MOQ guarantee.

Can I Review A Digital Proof?

Ask for a digital artwork proof in your brief. Proof scope, cost, revision allowances and timing are agreed for each project.

Which Artwork Should I Provide?

Upload JPG, PNG, PDF or ZIP files with your quote enquiry (up to 3 files, 2 MB total), or share an accessible file link. Include dimensions, placement and color references. Vector artwork is useful when available; a clear reference image can start the discussion.

How Do I Choose Materials And Sizes?

Confirm fiber composition, fabric weight, measurements and tolerances for the selected product. Images and selectable sizes do not replace an approved specification sheet.

How Long Does Delivery Take?

Provide the destination and required arrival date. Digital proof review, approvals, production and shipping need separate allowance. The schedule is confirmed with your quotation.

What About Returns Or Product Issues?

Confirm return arrangements for standard products before purchase. Agree custom specifications and issue-resolution terms before approval. Contact us with the order reference and photographs if a concern arises.

Can You Meet A Testing Or Environmental Standard?

State the exact standard and documentation required. Certifications, material content and testing scope must be verified for the specific product; no blanket certification is claimed.

Does The Form Send Automatically?

Yes. Submit the form to send your requirements to our team. The status message confirms success or explains how to retry.

DECORATION TECHNIQUES

Finishes That Bring Your Design To Life.

Explore decoration methods for your custom product. The right option depends on the product, material and design.

Screen Printing

Choose plastisol, water-based or rubber ink to suit the artwork and product.

Puff Printing

A raised ink effect brings selected parts of a design forward.

DTG Printing

Direct-to-garment printing reproduces detailed, multicolor artwork on suitable fabric products.

Heat Transfers

Offset and film transfers reproduce crisp artwork on suitable product surfaces.

Sublimation

Sublimation bonds color into suitable polyester-based materials for all-over or placed artwork.

Embroidery

Flat, 3D or combined embroidery can highlight selected areas of a design.

Metallic Foil

Gold or silver foil creates a bright, reflective accent.

Special Effects

Add a standout finish with reflective, glow-in-the-dark or fluorescent details.

PRODUCT NOTES

Spot The Choices That Bring A Product Together.

Good references do more than set a mood. They help clarify a silhouette, surface, color relationship or detail that can be carried into a specification.

This edit looks at four useful prompts: garment character, texture, headwear and packaging. Use what fits your project, then confirm the choices against your own brief.

EDITORIAL PROMPTS

Four Ways To Make An Idea More Specific.

APPARELStart With The SilhouetteMATERIALBring Texture Into The BriefHEADWEARDesign Around The PanelPACKAGINGFinish The Full Presentation

NOTES FOR YOUR NEXT PROJECT

Signals Shaping The Brief

These are creative prompts, not market forecasts. Adapt what is useful to your product, audience and production requirements.

APPAREL / IDENTITY

Build A Club Capsule Around One Anchor.

Choose one garment or graphic to carry the strongest identity, then let the other pieces support it. A shared color story, consistent placement and a considered size range can make a small assortment feel connected.

Put In The Brief

List each garment, decoration location, artwork version, size and color mix. If a mark appears on more than one item, note whether its dimensions change.

MATERIAL / FINISH

Let The Surface Do Some Of The Work.

When a product already has a noticeable texture, consider how decoration will sit against it. Contrast can add clarity; a quieter treatment can leave the material in focus.

Put In The Brief

Share a close reference for the surface, finished artwork size, color direction and any fine lines or lettering that need review.

HEADWEAR / PLACEMENT

Design Around The Panel.

A cap front is curved and divided by seams. Panel shape, profile and decoration placement affect how a graphic reads at its finished size.

Put In The Brief

Include the cap profile, closure preference, artwork size and approximate placement. A mockup can help compare the mark with seams and curves.

PRESENTATION / PACKAGING

Think About First Look And Handoff.

Labels and packaging affect how a product is stored, shipped, grouped or presented. Consider these details alongside the item itself.

Put In The Brief

Note the packing unit, labels, inserts, protection and delivery destination requirements you already know.

KEEP THE IDEAS CLOSE

Save The Notes And Shape A Product Brief.

Use the digest as a working reference. When you are ready, share your product, quantity range and delivery needs with Netpro.
